ranking_metric: deps.dev directDependentCount summed over all releases
selection: JCodec (76), MP3SPI (55), JLayer (33), and jaudiotagger (8) have comparable summed deps.dev direct-dependent metrics and exact outputs on two valid untagged Layer III controls. The first three decode PCM; jaudiotagger is selected only for correct first-frame MPEG header fields, with no decoding or whole-stream claim. Each has own Java parser source-line coverage and stable parser-derived AFL++ feedback.
family_note: JCodec and JLayer are independent decoders. MP3SPI has its own Java Sound reader/converter but delegates to the JLayer fork. jaudiotagger has its own MPEGFrameHeader code, already present as the same package in the tagged-MP3 cell; jid3lib and mp3agic share historical project ancestry.
uncertainty: Four pure-Java Layer III paths verified; no padding. jaudiotagger is header-only and its higher-level MP3AudioHeader(File) misidentifies the valid 22.05 kHz control start at byte 104 and estimates 5 rather than 12 frames; the selected first-header API reports only independently correct fields. Maven Central phrase queries returned no hits, so named leads were inspected via deps.dev and package documentation. deps.dev counts whole-package dependency use, not MP3-specific calls. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5 or ID3 behavior. Java SE 25 exports no MP3 reader by inventory.
